findings.title: CORS policy reflects an arbitrary Origin
findings.description: The server echoed back an unrecognized probe origin ('https://untrusted-probe.httpsec-auditor.example') verbatim in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials allowed. This effectively allows any website to make cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the response using the victim's session cookies.
findings.remediation: Validate the Origin header against an explicit allowlist server-side before reflecting it; never reflect unknown origins, especially alongside Allow-Credentials.

findings.title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security header
findings.description: Without HSTS, browsers will happily follow a plain-HTTP link or attacker-injected redirect to this host, enabling SSL-stripping attacks on the first request.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' is missing the Secure flag
findings.description: Without Secure, the cookie can be sent over a plaintext HTTP connection, exposing it to network eavesdroppers.
findings.remediation: Add `Secure` to the Set-Cookie attributes for 'sessionid'.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' is missing the HttpOnly flag
findings.description: Without HttpOnly, client-side JavaScript (including injected via XSS) can read this cookie's value.
findings.remediation: Add `HttpOnly` to the Set-Cookie attributes for 'sessionid' unless a script genuinely needs to read it.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: Without a CSP, the browser has no defense-in-depth against injected scripts if an XSS bug exists elsewhere on the page.
findings.remediation: Define a restrictive CSP (start with `default-src 'self'`) and tighten per-resource.

findings.title: No clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors)
findings.description: The page can be embedded in a hidden/opaque iframe on an attacker's site, enabling clickjacking.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' has no SameSite attribute
findings.description: Without SameSite, the cookie is sent on cross-site requests, widening exposure to CSRF.

findings.title: Cookie 'cart_id' is missing the Secure flag
findings.description: Without Secure, the cookie can be sent over a plaintext HTTP connection, exposing it to network eavesdroppers.
findings.remediation: Add `Secure` to the Set-Cookie attributes for 'cart_id'.

findings.title: Cookie 'cart_id' is missing the HttpOnly flag
findings.description: Without HttpOnly, client-side JavaScript (including injected via XSS) can read this cookie's value.
findings.remediation: Add `HttpOnly` to the Set-Cookie attributes for 'cart_id' unless a script genuinely needs to read it.

findings.title: Cookie 'cart_id' has no SameSite attribute
findings.description: Without SameSite, the cookie is sent on cross-site requests, widening exposure to CSRF.

findings.title: TLS certificate expires in 8 day(s)
findings.description: The certificate is approaching its expiry date.
findings.remediation: Renew the certificate before it expires to avoid a browser trust failure.

findings.title: Missing or invalid X-Content-Type-Options header
findings.description: Without `nosniff`, browsers may MIME-sniff a response into an executable content type.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy header
findings.description: Without an explicit policy, full URLs (potentially containing tokens/paths) may leak to third parties via the Referer header.

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy header
findings.description: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, etc.) are not explicitly restricted.
findings.remediation: Send a `Permissions-Policy` header disabling features the site doesn't use.

findings.title: Server header discloses server/framework details
findings.description: `Server: nginx/1.18.0` helps an attacker fingerprint the stack and target version-specific exploits.
findings.remediation: Suppress or genericize the `Server` header at the web server/proxy layer.
